members.position: [THEORY] Ship a fork-first, optional generic credential-broker seam, with an aigate adapter outside the core provider and dynamic resolution at Claude query/session creation; do not implement a zero-diff wrapper because T3 must report limits and preserve event-sourced state. [VERIFIED] Use per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and child env injection, select the best-headroom Claude account at session start, park on typed quota failures, and hop only at a turn boundary by recreating the SDK query with its resume cursor. [THEORY] Represent native Claude, Muse, and Kimi K3 as versioned T3-side route profiles rather than aigate-discovered models; Claude is the only brokered provider in v1, while Codex, Cursor, Grok, and OpenCode remain unchanged. [THEORY] Monday's smallest step is an integration spike that proves SDK identity with account A versus conflicting Keychain account B, then adds a no-op broker interface plus an aigate selector test before any client UI work.

claims.claim: T3's current Claude environment path creates a per-instance environment object rather than mutating the server-global process environment, so concurrent provider instances do not inherently overwrite one another's credentials.
claims.evidence: Chair verification EXP-4: mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment() in apps/server/src/provider/ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:3-16 spreads into a new object; it is called by Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:128, and ClaudeAdapter.ts:4176 passes the resulting env to query().

claims.claim: The Agent SDK maintains one long-lived query per T3 thread, but T3 has a resume-cursor path that can create a new query for a later turn.
claims.evidence: Chair verification EXP-3: ClaudeAdapter.ts createQuery() at approximately :4221 stores ClaudeSessionContext instances around :4280; readClaudeResumeState, resume, and resumeSessionAt support recreating a query from a prior session.

claims.claim: Account hopping should be implemented only at a turn boundary in v1, not during a streamed turn.
claims.evidence: EXP-3 establishes the long-lived query and resume mechanism; aigate-run.sh changes accounts by launching a new process and continuing. A mid-stream credential change could duplicate or lose tool effects.
claims.test: Run a disposable two-account test that exhausts account A after a partial tool interaction, recreates the query with account B and the resume cursor, and verifies no duplicated tool calls, lost context, or protocol corruption.

claims.claim: T3 already receives rate-limit telemetry that can drive limit reporting and account parking without parsing human-readable CLI output.
claims.evidence: Chair verification EXP-5: SDK rate_limit_event messages are mapped to account.rate-limits.updated orchestration events in ClaudeAdapter.ts:3507-3552.

claims.claim: aigate's current selector is suitable for coarse best-headroom selection but is not a lease or transaction, so per-turn selection across many hosts may assign the same account concurrently.
claims.evidence: aigate src/server.js:295-298 implements pickRanked; the supplied inspection found no lease/transaction, and /api/select returns an account plus setup_token using caller-supplied exclusions.
claims.test: Issue parallel /api/select requests from multiple hosts, record duplicate assignments, and measure whether parking and polling recover within the configured TTL.

claims.claim: Muse and Kimi K3 should be modeled as T3-side route profiles with explicit environment overlays, not as ordinary Anthropic account selections.
claims.evidence: aigate-muse.sh requires api.meta.ai, bearer authentication, all-tier model mapping, a 1,007,997 context limit, and a tool-name workaround; Kimi likewise uses a separate Anthropic-compatible endpoint and auth family. aigate has no model endpoint.
claims.test: Implement native Claude, Muse, and Kimi profiles and verify model-picker entries, endpoint/auth isolation, context behavior, tier mapping, tool compatibility, and successful probes for each profile.

claims.claim: aigate cannot provide model listing today, because /api/capabilities reports provider key counts and Claude account counts but no model identifiers.
claims.evidence: Operator and chair repository inspection: aigate/src/providers.js is a provider-key catalog; no /api/models endpoint exists; /api/capabilities contains registry counts and selectable Claude-account counts only.

claims.claim: The broker must be generic and optional, with a no-op implementation preserving current behavior and an aigate adapter configured by user-supplied URL and secret rather than a hardcoded LAN address.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md requires optional, generic, remote-ready integrations; T3 already provides ProviderInstanceEnvironmentVariable sensitive storage through packages/contracts/src/providerInstance.ts:104-113 and ServerSecretStore in serverSettings.ts:316-376.
claims.test: Run the full provider and session test suites with the broker disabled and compare behavior against the pre-broker baseline; run an aigate outage test and confirm fail-closed behavior without secret leakage or silent fallback to the wrong account.

claims.claim: Claude is the only provider with aigate account rotation in v1; Codex, Cursor, Grok, and OpenCode receive explicit no-integration decisions.
claims.evidence: The supplied aigate API is Claude-specific: /api/select returns Claude setup tokens and /api/accounts exposes Anthropic rate-limit state. The GPT rung was retired on 2026-08-04, and no non-Claude account-selection contract was found.

claims.claim: The fork-first posture is justified, but acceptance of a later upstream generic hook remains unknown rather than established.
claims.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md reportedly says the project is not actively accepting contributions, while maintainers accept only small focused PRs; this supports a fork or external package but does not prove a minimal generic hook would be rejected.
claims.test: After the fork proves the seam, submit a narrowly scoped provider-agnostic spawn-time credential-resolver proposal with no aigate references and record maintainer disposition.

challenges.their_claim: [THEORY] The Monday step can add useAigate and call /api/select during instantiation, with Muse and Kimi left as manually configured instances.
challenges.problem: [VERIFIED] EXP-4 shows Claude environment is captured at adapter construction and reused for the long-lived query, so construction-time selection cannot support account hopping or reliable per-turn re-selection. [THEORY] Manual Muse/Kimi instances may work, but the route-specific context, tier, and tool settings need a first-class profile to prevent unsafe partial configuration.
challenges.test: Trace and test a turn after an account is parked; if the active adapter does not recreate query options with a newly selected token, construction-time selection is insufficient.

challenges.their_claim: [THEORY] No T3 broker concept should be added until the Keychain experiment runs, and a sidecar can keep three dumb Claude instances working.
challenges.problem: [VERIFIED] The chair's EXP-1 and addendum show the same Claude binary honors CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN under a fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and EXP-4 proves per-instance env objects are concurrency-safe. [UNMEASURED] The exact Agent SDK query identity still requires confirmation, but delaying all architectural work until that result conflates one authentication-risk test with the already-established need for dynamic query recreation and limit events.
challenges.test: Run query() through probeClaudeCapabilities with conflicting Keychain and injected credentials; use init.account identity and captured request credentials as the discriminator.

challenges.their_claim: [THEORY] Mid-thread hopping can resume under T3 because aigate-run.sh proves claude --continue preserves the conversation.
challenges.problem: [VERIFIED] The CLI's --continue behavior is not proof of Agent SDK resume correctness after streamed tool calls; EXP-3 proves only that a resume cursor exists. Treating the paths as equivalent risks duplicated side effects.
challenges.test: Force a controlled quota failure after a tool call, recreate the SDK query with resume and account B, and compare tool-call IDs, side effects, and transcript continuity.

challenges.their_claim: [THEORY] Phase 1 can map alternate endpoints into distinct provider instances using existing environment injection with no broker concept.
challenges.problem: [VERIFIED] This supports route configuration but not account selection, limit reporting, parking, or account hopping. A zero-broker phase is a useful smoke test, not the complete integration plan requested by the council.
challenges.test: Demonstrate selection, telemetry, quota parking, and turn-boundary re-selection in T3 while preserving route-specific Muse/Kimi environments.

challenges.their_claim: [THEORY] The integration should resemble aigate-run.sh closely enough to provide automatic retries and account hopping inside T3.
challenges.problem: [VERIFIED] aigate-run.sh classifies CLI text and relaunches processes, whereas T3 consumes SDK events through a long-lived query. Directly transplanting the wrapper would not satisfy typed event reporting and could retry after partial tool execution.
challenges.test: Inject synthetic 429, 529, and partial-stream failures into the SDK adapter and verify that each is classified into safe retry, park-and-hop, or user-visible failure without duplicate effects.

retractions.was: [CONTESTED] I previously treated credential precedence under T3's Agent SDK and isolated config as wholly unmeasured.
retractions.now: [VERIFIED with residual uncertainty] The same spawned Claude binary honors an injected OAuth token under a fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and the chair's addendum says this is the practical SDK code path; only direct query() identity confirmation and future-version behavior remain unmeasured.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-1 and its addendum supplied the missing controlled bogus-token/live-token evidence.

retractions.was: [THEORY] I previously proposed deferring account hopping until the query lifecycle was investigated.
retractions.now: [VERIFIED architecture, THEORY safety] EXP-3 establishes one long-lived query per thread and an available resume cursor, so turn-boundary hop is now the concrete implementation target; safety after partial tool execution remains a testable theory.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-3 supplied direct ClaudeAdapter lifecycle and resume-state findings.

retractions.was: [CONTESTED] I previously described dynamic environment resolution as potentially available through the existing seam.
retractions.now: [VERIFIED] Environment is captured at adapter construction and reused for query options; dynamic broker resolution requires new code or adapter reconstruction.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-4 traced makeClaudeEnvironment and queryOptions.env in ClaudeAdapter.ts.

needs_research: Does direct @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() expose init.account identity matching the injected aigate account under a conflicting macOS Keychain login?
Which exact T3 contract events, projectors, and web/desktop/mobile components should represent broker selecting, active, parked, exhausted, reauth-required, unavailable, and disabled states?
What typed SDK event or error preserves HTTP 429, 529, quota, and retry-after information for safe classification?
Does SDK resume across two Claude Max accounts preserve transcript and tool idempotency after a partial streamed turn?
What is the maintainer response to a narrowly scoped provider-agnostic credential-resolver hook?
members.dissent: I cannot yet agree that account hopping is safe or that the exact first-class contract surface is settled. The deciding tests are direct query() credential-identity verification and a two-account resume test after a partial tool call; until both pass, v1 must select at session start and fail visibly at exhaustion rather than promise seamless mid-thread hopping.

members.position: We should implement an upstreamable, generic CredentialBroker interface in apps/server/src/provider/ with an optional aigate adapter. Account selection occurs at session start and turn boundaries via GET /api/select, using T3's turn-based resume cursor (resumeSessionAt) to execute account hops without lost state, while SDK rate_limit_events trigger POST /api/events/limit telemetry. Non-Anthropic models (Muse, Kimi) belong as static route profiles in T3's ClaudeProvider catalog that automatically apply required env flags (e.g., CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1007997), since aigate has no model listing API. V1 focuses exclusively on Claude; Codex, Cursor, Grok, and OpenCode remain no-op given aigate's retired non-Claude pools.

members.position: EXP-1 killed the Keychain blocker: with per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, injected CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN wins and you do not touch the developer's login. Stop designing CredentialBroker cathedrals. v1 is three dumb Claude instances (or one instance whose env is re-resolved only when you rebuild the adapter) fed by an optional external select call — multi-instance is already the account primitive. Muse/Kimi stay T3-side static route/env profiles; aigate has no models API. Codex/Cursor/Grok/OpenCode: no. Mid-thread hop is kill-query+resume with new env (EXP-3), not magic, and env is captured at adapter construction (EXP-4) so anyone promising per-turn select without rebuild is lying.

claims.claim: Under isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is honored and Keychain does not rescue a bogus token; T3 already sets per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR so aigate-style Keychain deletion is unnecessary.

claims.claim: Upstream will not land an aigate-named or large broker feature; keep aigate adapter fork/external.

claims.test: If ever upstreaming: PR only generic optional env-resolve hook, zero aigate strings; closed-as-policy ⇒ fork stays.

The polite furniture is 'we need a broker concept'; the impolite question is 'what line of code is missing after EXP-1/3/4/5?' — adapter rebuild on limit + optional select call.

members.position: T3 Code should integrate aigate as a credential broker in a fork-first approach, using the existing per-instance env injection seam (mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment) with per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolation, which chair EXP-1 VERIFIED avoids Keychain shadowing. The broker resolves at session start (not per-turn) by calling aigate /api/select and injecting the token into the instance's environment. Model listing for Muse/Kimi is a T3-side static route profile, not an aigate endpoint. Codex/Cursor/Grok/OpenCode are out of scope for v1. The Monday-shippable step: add an optional 'credentialBroker' config to Claude provider instances that specifies a broker URL/token, and on instance creation, call the broker and inject the returned env vars. This is a small, reversible fork feature that can be upstreamed later if the maintainers accept a generic hook.

challenges.their_claim: THEORY: A first release should call aigate at process/session start and inject the selected Claude OAuth token, rather than attempting per-turn account switching.
challenges.problem: Agreed on session-start injection, but the claim assumes the env seam is refreshed per spawn. EXP-4 shows makeClaudeEnvironment runs once per adapter construction, not per query. So session-start injection requires a new per-spawn resolution point or a re-creation of the adapter/instance. The claim does not account for this static capture.
challenges.test: Instrument ClaudeDriver to log the env hash on each sendTurn across a 3-turn thread. If the hash is identical, the env is not refreshed per spawn, and per-turn account switching without re-creation is not possible.

challenges.their_claim: Phase 2 introduces an upstreamable lightweight CredentialBroker interface that dynamically invokes aigate's /api/select and /api/events/limit endpoints on session init and retry.
challenges.problem: Upstreamability is contested: CONTRIBUTING.md states 'not actively accepting contributions'. The claim that a CredentialBroker interface would be accepted as a small PR is unsupported by any evidence of maintainer openness. Until that is tested, the upstreamable claim is a theory at best.
challenges.test: Submit a minimal PR adding only the CredentialBroker interface (no aigate-specific code) and observe maintainer response. If closed, the fork-first path is mandatory.

challenges.their_claim: THEORY: Zero broker concept in T3 core — use three dumb Claude instances whose env secrets an external aigate side-car refreshes.
challenges.problem: This design requires the side-car to modify T3's secret store (ServerSecretStore) out-of-band, which is a race condition with T3's own settings management. T3's secret store is not designed for external mutation; it's write-once from the UI. The side-car would need to either restart T3 services or use an undocumented API, breaking the 'remote-ready' requirement. Also, model listing for Muse/Kimi would be entirely manual per instance, offering no user experience improvement over current manual config.
challenges.test: Implement the side-car approach: have an external process write new tokens into ~/.t3/userdata/secrets/*.bin and then trigger a provider instance re-initialization. Measure whether the instance picks up the new token without restarting the server or losing session state. If it cannot, the side-car approach is insufficient for dynamic rotation.

challenges.their_claim: If mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment() overlays onto the server-global process.env, then two broker-backed instances on different accounts race.
challenges.problem: EXP-4 VERIFIED that mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment does NOT mutate process.env; it creates a new object per instance. The claim was based on ambiguous wording in the brief, but the actual code is concurrency-safe.
challenges.test: Read ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:3-16 (14 lines) — the code spreads into a new object, not process.env. No race.

challenges.their_claim: The integration must hit all surfaces (web/desktop/mobile) and provide model listing for non-Anthropic models.
challenges.problem: Model listing is conflated with credential brokering. aigate has no model endpoint; Muse/Kimi require static route profiles. Requiring model listing from aigate invents scope. The integration should separate credential brokering (aigate's job) from model discovery (T3's static catalog or future provider capability).
challenges.test: Implement T3-side static route profiles for Muse/Kimi and verify they work without any aigate model endpoint. Compare UX: user creates a Claude instance with predefined env overrides vs. querying a server for available models. The simpler approach is sufficient for v1.

members.dissent: I cannot agree to a design that either (a) embeds aigate-specific code in T3 core or (b) requires a new aigate models endpoint. The minimum viable integration is a generic spawn-time env resolution hook in the Claude provider that can be backed by aigate or any other external selector. This hook should be optional and off by default. I also dissent from the assumption that mid-session account hopping is safe without testing the SDK's resume mechanism with a changed env. The 'session-boundary only' approach is safer and should be the default. Finally, I disagree that model listing is a v1 requirement; Muse/Kimi can be statically configured as provider instances with custom env, which is already possible today.

members.position: Both zero-code gates I demanded last round have now run and passed: EXP-4 proves the env seam is race-free but static per adapter construction, and EXP-1 proves an injected CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN wins under an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (bogus token 401s — no Keychain rescue). The design is therefore: a fork-first, opt-in broker resolved once per session at query construction (the verified attachment point, since one query() lives per thread per EXP-3), with aigate as an external adapter behind a no-op default, and Muse/Kimi as static route-profile pseudo-models whose pass-through EXP-6 mechanically verifies. Account hopping collapses to one precisely-defined mechanism — park via /api/events/limit, kill the query, recreate with the existing resume cursor and fresh env — and it ships GATED, because cross-account resume through the SDK is the single remaining load-bearing unknown (experiment E2 below). The warden's Keychain deletion is dead: unnecessary under per-instance config isolation, and it must not be ported into an open-source product. v1 is Claude-only; Codex/Cursor/Grok/OpenCode get explicit 'unsupported' decisions with the verified reason (no aigate pools, gpt rung retired 2026-08-04) on record. Monday: three zero-diff experiments — SDK-path token confirmation via the existing probeClaudeCapabilities, E2 cross-account resume, E3 rate-limit payload capture — then the first contract diff.

The concurrency hazard I raised against the brief last round does not exist.

claims.claim: Under an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, an env-injected token is honored and a stored login does not override or rescue it: bogus token → 401 'OAuth access token is invalid'; live aigate setup_token → success. Residual caveat I am required to state: the harness was the CLI with -p, not the SDK query() literal path; the chair's same-binary argument (pathToClaudeCodeExecutable → same cli, same env forwarding) is strong but the SDK-specific probe remains undone first-hand.

claims.claim: One long-lived SDK query() per thread (createQuery at ClaudeAdapter.ts:4221, sessions Map at :4280), and a resume-cursor mechanism exists (resume: <uuid>, resumeSessionAt). Account hop mid-thread is therefore exactly: kill query → recreate with resume cursor + new env, at a turn boundary. It is NOT a per-turn spawn swap.
claims.evidence: Chair EXP-3, repo citations above.

claims.claim: Cross-account resume through the SDK — session uuid minted under account A, resumed via query() with account B's token and a fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — is unproven. The warden proves claude --continue cross-account at the interactive CLI level (operational evidence only); the SDK resume path under a swapped env is a different code path and nobody has run it.
claims.evidence: EXP-3 establishes the mechanism exists in-adapter; nothing in the chair's passes exercises it across accounts. This is now the single load-bearing unknown for the brief's requirement (a) 'hopping accounts when one runs dry'.
claims.test: E2 (zero T3 diffs, scratch script on the SDK directly): query() under aigate token A on a throwaway thread; capture session uuid; interrupt; recreate query() with resume: uuid, env carrying token B from /api/select?exclude=A, fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Assert: no auth/session-identity error, reply demonstrates continuity, and probeClaudeCapabilities-style init.account.email reads B. Pass → hop ungates. Fail → v1 is session-start selection only and the brief's 'hop' requirement is declared unmet-with-evidence.

challenges.their_claim: Zero-diff v1: three dumb Claude instances whose env secrets an external aigate sidecar refreshes — no broker code in T3 at all.
challenges.problem: EXP-4 cuts both ways and Mouse has not absorbed it: env is captured ONCE at adapter construction, so a sidecar that rewrites the secret materialization does not propagate — new sessions keep the stale token unless an instance-env update triggers an adapter rebuild, which nobody has established. As written the sidecar plan either silently serves dead accounts or requires server restarts as its rotation cadence, which fails the moment shoemoney-weekly-max happens mid-day. What survives of the plan, stated precisely: zero-diff v0 = one instance per aigate account with static sensitive tokens, user picks the instance per thread — that is manual selection, not brokering, and it cannot hop at all. Also, Mouse's headline blocker ('keychain hazard UNMEASURED, everything else is fanfic') is stale: EXP-1 ran it.
challenges.test: Change a sensitive env var on a live provider instance, start a new thread, read init.account.email. If it still shows the old account, the sidecar needs an instance-reload trigger (new code or manual UX) and the 'zero-diff' claim is falsified as stated.

challenges.their_claim: Integration touches <5 server files via a useAigate boolean; aigate's hop logic 'does not map' to T3 because no --continue flag exists; model listing out of scope.
challenges.problem: Three defects. (1) '<5 files' is irreconcilable with the brief's own doctrine: contracts in packages/contracts, reverse states projected for web/desktop/mobile, and docs are required surfaces — a boolean on ClaudeProvider with no broker-state events gives the event-sourced clients nothing to project and fails requirement (a) 'reporting limits back'. Either scope honestly to fork-only or recount. (2) 'Does not map' is falsified as stated: EXP-3's resume cursor is the in-adapter isomorph of --continue; the correct label is 'mapped mechanically, unmeasured cross-account' (E2). (3) 'Probe headroom before each turn via /api/accounts and skip an instance' contradicts EXP-4: env is bound at construction, so per-turn instance skipping changes nothing about which token the live query holds — T3-side headroom awareness comes from EXP-5's typed events, not pre-turn polling.
challenges.test: E2 settles (2). For (1), enumerate the actual diff against the doctrine checklist (contracts, decider/projector events, three clients, docs) and count files — if the count exceeds 5, amend the claim. (3) is settled textually by EXP-4.

challenges.their_claim: Phase 2 broker 'dynamically invokes aigate's /api/select and /api/events/limit on session init and retry'.
challenges.problem: The session-init limb is now verified-sound (EXP-1, EXP-4). The 'and retry' limb silently assumes mid-session account switch works; per EXP-3 it requires kill-query + recreate-with-resume, and cross-account resume via the SDK is UNMEASURED. Shipping the retry limb before E2 risks stranding live threads at exactly the moment the user is most blocked (account exhausted). Gate it, or Phase 2 ships the riskiest half first.
challenges.test: E2 as specified in my claims. Pass → retry limb ungates with the kill+resume shape; fail → Phase 2 is session-init selection only, and exhaustion surfaces as a projected 'parked/reauth-needed' state prompting a new session — which the event-sourced clients can at least render honestly.

challenges.their_claim: Requirement (a): 'picking the Claude account with the most headroom per turn/session'.
challenges.problem: Per-turn account selection is architecturally unavailable as stated: EXP-3 (one long-lived query per thread) plus EXP-4 (env frozen at construction) mean changing accounts mid-thread REQUIRES killing and recreating the query — per-turn selection would mean a kill+resume cycle every turn: expensive, pointless, and dependent on the unmeasured E2. The honest granularity is per-SESSION selection plus hop-on-exhaustion (gated). The brief should be amended so the plan is reviewed against what the code permits, not an aspiration.
challenges.test: None needed — settled textually by EXP-3 and EXP-4. Amendment is a wording fix; E2 then determines whether 'hop-on-exhaustion' joins 'per-session' in the shipped granularity.

Env is static at construction (EXP-4) so pure external file refresh without rebuild does nothing to a live adapter.

retractions.was: TANK claimed: 'UNMEASURED: aigate-run.sh's keychain-delete trick... may not apply under Agent SDK with per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — but it is UNMEASURED.'
retractions.now: VERIFIED: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env beats Keychain when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is isolated per-instance (EXP-1). No Keychain clearing needed. The shadowing hazard is resolved for the SDK path with per-instance isolation.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-1 provided conclusive evidence on the same binary the SDK spawns. The Keychain outranking is specific to the default config dir, not T3's isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

retractions.was: TANK claimed: 'mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment overlays onto process.env' (implying possible concurrency race).
retractions.now: VERIFIED: mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment does NOT mutate process.env; it creates a new object per instance (EXP-4). No race.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-4 explicitly read the code and confirmed it spreads into a new object. The brief's wording was ambiguous; the actual code is safe.

retractions.was: If mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment overlays onto server-global process.env, two broker-backed instances race and last writer wins — the seam may be concurrency-unsafe for exactly its recommended use case.
retractions.now: No race exists: the function spreads into a fresh object (ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:11) and env is captured per adapter; concurrent instances on different accounts cannot clobber each other.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-4 read the 14 lines directly — the experiment I named ('read ProviderInstanceEnvironment.ts:3-16, settles it textually') was run and settled against the hazard.

retractions.was: Whether a stored login outranks injected CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN under the Agent SDK with per-instance CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is UNMEASURED (my E1) and blocks all design.
retractions.now: Resolved for design purposes: under isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR the env token wins (bogus → 401, no Keychain rescue; live aigate token → success). No Keychain deletion anywhere in the design. I retain one residual: the literal harness was CLI -p, so an SDK-path confirmation probe stays on the Monday list as a 10-minute verification, not a blocker.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-1 plus the same-binary addendum (pathToClaudeCodeExecutable spawns the cli that was tested; Linux .credentials.json isolation follows by construction).

retractions.was: Mid-thread account hopping works IF the adapter spawns per turn — park, re-select, next spawn picks up the new account.
retractions.now: The antecedent is false: EXP-3 shows one long-lived query() per thread. Hop = kill query + recreate with the existing resume cursor + new env, at a turn boundary. Whether that resume works CROSS-ACCOUNT is the new UNMEASURED (E2), and hop ships gated on it.
retractions.because: Chair EXP-3 (createQuery :4221, sessions Map :4280, resume/resumeSessionAt mechanism) — proof I had not considered that the mechanism exists but the spawn model differs from my assumption.
